summary: Hermann Kulke works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras, Freiburg under Ulrich Schneider and Hermann Goetz, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg (1967–1988) and Kiel University as Chair of Asian History (1988–2003).

Hermann Lommel was an Indologist, Iranian and Central Asian scholar, and linguist. He studied in Munich and Göttingen under Jacob Wackernagel, Friedrich Carl Andreas, and Hermann Oldenberg. He taught at Göttingen (1915–1920) and Frankfurt (1920–1950).

Hermann Mittelberger was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna and later held posts at Vienna, Würzburg, Utrecht, and the University of Graz, where he was professor of comparative Indo-European from 1971 to 2003.

Hermann Møller was a linguist. He studied at Kiel, Munich, Berlin, Breslau, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius, completing his PhD in 1875. He later held Privatdozent posts at Kiel University (1878) and the University of Copenhagen (1883).

Hermann Oesterley, a scholar in Indology and other fields, studied at the University of Music and Theatre Leipzig and Göttingen (PhD ~1855). He served at Kiel University (1858–1861), Göttingen State Library (1862–1872), and Wrocław University Library (1873–1891).

Hermann Oldenberg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Berlin (1878), Kiel University as Ordinarius (1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen as Professor from 1908.

Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel and Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Bonn, Tübingen, Berlin, and Leipzig under Usener, Gildemeister, Roth, Weber, Curtius, and Leskien. He served at Leipzig (1875) and as Ordinarius and director at Heidelberg University from 1877.

Hermann Paul was a linguist who studied at Berlin under Heymann Steinthal and Leipzig under Friedrich Zarncke, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1874–1877) and the University of Munich (1893–1916).

Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied under Bernhard Hirzel and completed a doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He served at the University of Zurich (1833) and the University of Göttingen (1855).

Hermann Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at Munich (~1848) and held a Lehrauftrag at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1851.

Hermann Usener was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn (~1854–1858), and later held posts at the universities of Bern (~1861–1863), Greifswald (~1863–1866), and Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Walter was an Indologist. He studied at Neuchâtel, Edinburgh, Tübingen, and Munich, where he earned a PhD under Ernst Kuhn in 1893. From 1900 to 1936, he served as lecturer and professor at McGill University.

Hermann Weller was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He later held posts at Tübingen as Privatdozent in 1930 and as honorary professor from 1938 to 1952.

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and Franz Bopp. He taught at Beheim-Schwarzbach'sche Realschule, Gymnasium Schneidemühl, and became professor at Berlin in 1872.
Hertha Krick was an Indologist. She completed her PhD under Gerhard Oberhammer at the University of Vienna (~1965–1972), where she subsequently served as an assistant from 1972 to 1979.

Hervey DeWitt Griswold was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Union College, Union Theological Seminary, Oxford, Berlin, and Cornell. He was Professor of Philosophy at Forman Christian College (1894–1914) and Visiting Lecturer at Columbia (1923–1929).

Hew McLeod was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago (~1950–1954), and SOAS University of London (~1963–1965), and held a Redaktionsråd post at Otago (~1971–1997).

Heymann Steinthal was a linguist and philosopher who studied at Berlin under August Boeckh (~1843–1847). He served at Frederick William University / Humboldt University of Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and held a researcher post there (attested 1995).
